Starting certainty for all outcomes is **LOW** (observational evidence). Post-Block-9 corpus: 251 studies (14 RCTs), 525 arms. ## Summary {#sec-grade-summary} ::: {#tbl-grade-summary .cell tbl-cap='GRADE certainty of evidence — all outcomes, both comparisons. All C1 outcomes stable in direction and certainty. ::: ## Domain-Level Assessments {#sec-grade-domains} ### Overall Survival ::: {#tbl-grade-os .cell tbl-cap='GRADE domain assessment — Overall Survival.'} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Domain, ~C1, ~C2, "Study design", "39 retro/registry + 1 RCT; start LOW", "All retro/registry; start LOW", "Risk of bias", "No downgrade (effect survives M2)", "No downgrade (M2 OR 0.82 still protective)", "Inconsistency", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 64%; \u03c4 = 0.61)", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 95%; one registry dominant)", "Indirectness", "0", "0", "Imprecision", "0 (CrI excludes null; N = 19,724)", "0 (CrI excludes null; N = 12,851)", "Pub. bias", "0", "0", "Upgrade", "0", "+1 (cross-comparison coherence; sensitivity k=21 strengthens)", "Net", "\u22121", "0", "CERTAINTY", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW" ) |> kable() |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

The pre-Block-9 C2 NRM estimate (k = 5, OR 0.65 [0.43–0.97]) should be interpreted with caution given the arm classification issues that reduced k. ### aGVHD Grade II–IV ::: {#tbl-grade-agvhd .cell tbl-cap='GRADE domain assessment — aGVHD.'} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Domain, ~C1, ~C2, "Study design", "All retro/registry; start LOW", "All retro/registry; start LOW", "Risk of bias", "0 (ascertainment bias opposes effect)", "0 (same reasoning)", "Inconsistency", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 62%; \u03c4 = 0.68)", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 73%; \u03c4 = 0.55)", "Indirectness", "0", "0", "Imprecision", "0 (CrI excludes null; k = 28)", "0 (CrI excludes null; k = 9)", "Pub. bias", "\u22121 (Egger p = 0.041; T&F: 0.61 \u2192 0.83)", "0 (not assessable, k = 9)", "Upgrade", "+1 (confounders oppose effect; cross-comparison)", "+1 (confounders oppose; cross-comparison; sens k=14 consistent)", "Net", "\u22121", "0", "CERTAINTY", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW" ) |> kable() |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

Trim-and-fill imputes 8 studies, shifting the frequentist OR from 0.61 to 0.83 [0.61–1.13]. C1 aGVHD is accordingly downgraded to **VERY LOW**. The C2 aGVHD estimate (OR 0.58, k = 9) is too small for formal bias assessment but remains consistent. ### CMV Reactivation ::: {#tbl-grade-cmv .cell tbl-cap='GRADE domain assessment — CMV.'} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Domain, ~C1, ~C2, "Study design", "1 RCT + 21 retro; start LOW", "All retrospective; start LOW", "Risk of bias", "0 (monitoring protocol heterogeneity noted)", "0 (direction uncertain)", "Inconsistency", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 62%)", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 71%)", "Indirectness", "0", "0", "Imprecision", "0 (CrI excludes null [1.07\u20131.47])", "\u22121 (CrI crosses null [0.73\u20131.15])", "Upgrade", "+1 (steroid-independence; sensitivity convergence pattern)", "0 (see below)", "Net", "0", "\u22122", "CERTAINTY", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW" ) |> kable() |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

In the post-Block-9 corpus, C2 CMV has shifted to OR 0.92 [0.73–1.15], and the CrI crosses null. The binary reversal is no longer statistically credible. However, the **C2 sensitivity analysis** provides a different — and arguably stronger — form of evidence. When PTCy+ATG combination arms are reclassified as "PTCy-side" (k = 22), the CMV estimate converges to OR 1.00 [0.85–1.18]. This convergence is predicted by the depletion hierarchy: when both arms have deep T-cell depletion, CMV rates should equalise. The three estimates trace a gradient: | Analysis | Arms compared | OR | Interpretation | |---|---|---|---| | C1 primary | PTCy vs CNI | 1.26 | PTCy depletes more → more CMV | | C2 primary | PTCy vs ATG | 0.92 | Near-parity; slight PTCy advantage | | C2 sensitivity | PTCy+ATG vs ATG | 1.00 | Equal depletion → equal CMV | This gradient is more consistent with the depletion hierarchy than the pre-Block-9 binary reversal. The mechanistic conclusion — that CMV risk tracks T-cell depletion depth, not any PTCy-specific property — carries **LOW certainty** when assessed across the full evidence pattern, despite the individual C2 estimate being VERY LOW. ::: ### BSI and IFI ::: {#tbl-grade-infection .cell tbl-cap='GRADE domain assessment — BSI and IFI.'} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Domain, ~`C1 BSI`, ~`C1 IFI`, "Study design", "All retro/registry; start LOW", "All retro/registry; start LOW", "Risk of bias", "\u22121 (definitions heterogeneous)", "0", "Inconsistency", "\u22121 (I\u00B2 = 71%; freq CrI crosses null)", "\u22121 (\u03c4 = 1.64; I\u00B2 = 80%)", "Indirectness", "0", "0", "Imprecision", "0 (Bayes CrI excludes null)", "0 (CrI excludes null [0.29\u20130.63])", "Net", "\u22122", "\u22121", "CERTAINTY", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW" ) |> kable() |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

The Bayesian shrinkage prior and the frequentist random-effects model disagree, reducing confidence. IFI: The post-Block-9 estimate (OR 0.43 [0.29–0.63]) is substantially stronger than pre-Block-9 (0.73 [0.53–1.00]), but τ = 1.64 indicates extreme between-study heterogeneity. The frequentist CrI (0.21–1.74) again crosses null. With only k = 6 studies and this level of heterogeneity, the strong protective signal should be interpreted cautiously. ## Publication Bias {#sec-grade-pubbias} Formal assessment was conducted for C1 outcomes with k ≥ 10 using Egger's regression test and trim-and-fill. ::: {#tbl-grade-pubbias .cell tbl-cap='Publication bias assessment — C1 outcomes with k ≥ 10.'} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Outcome, ~k, ~`Egger z`, ~`Egger p`, ~`T&F imputed`, ~`Original OR`, ~`Adjusted OR`, "OS", 40, -1.02, 0.314, 7, "0.77 [0.66\u20130.90]", "0.86 [0.73\u20131.02]", "aGVHD", 28, -2.15, 0.041, 8, "0.61 [0.47\u20130.79]", "0.83 [0.61\u20131.13]", "CMV", 22, -0.21, 0.835, 0, "1.25 [0.94\u20131.66]", "1.25 [0.94\u20131.66]" ) |> mutate(`Egger p` = ifelse(`Egger p` < 0.05, paste0("**", sprintf("%.3f", `Egger p`), "**"), sprintf("%.3f", `Egger p`))) |> kable(align = c("l","r","r","r","r","c","c")) |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Outcome k Egger z Egger p T&F imputed Original OR Adjusted OR
OS 40 -1.02 0.314 7 0.77 [0.66–0.90] 0.86 [0.73–1.02]
aGVHD 28 -2.15 **0.041** 8 0.61 [0.47–0.79] 0.83 [0.61–1.13]
CMV 22 -0.21 0.835 0 1.25 [0.94–1.66] 1.25 [0.94–1.66]
````` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-warning} ## C1 aGVHD: Significant Funnel Asymmetry Egger's test detects significant small-study bias (p = 0.041). After trim-and-fill imputation, the adjusted OR shifts from 0.61 to 0.83 and the CI crosses null. The Bayesian pooled estimate (OR 0.67 [0.59–0.78]) is less extreme than the frequentist 0.61, reflecting shrinkage, but does not account for selective non-publication. C1 aGVHD certainty is downgraded from LOW to VERY LOW. C1 OS shows borderline concern: 7 studies imputed with adjusted OR touching null (0.86 [0.73–1.02]), though Egger's test is non-significant (p = 0.31). C1 CMV is symmetric with no imputed studies. ::: ## Narrative Summary {#sec-grade-narrative} Across both comparisons, certainty does not exceed LOW — a predictable consequence of an almost entirely observational evidence base. **The most robust finding** is C1 OS (OR 0.79, k = 40, LOW certainty), which has been stable across the pre-Block-9 and post-Block-9 analyses, is consistent across comparators (C2 OR 0.81), and has CrIs that exclude null. C1 aGVHD (OR 0.67, k = 28) is consistent across comparators (C2 OR 0.58, k = 9) and directionally stable, but is downgraded to VERY LOW due to significant funnel asymmetry (Egger p = 0.041). The trim-and-fill adjusted estimate (OR 0.83) crosses null, suggesting the effect size may be inflated by selective reporting of small positive studies. **Cross-comparison coherence** remains the strongest methodological asset. **The CMV depletion hierarchy** is supported not by a single direction reversal but by a three-point gradient across the primary and sensitivity analyses. This gradient pattern carries greater evidential weight than any one estimate. Certainty for the mechanistic conclusion (that CMV risk tracks depletion depth) is LOW when integrating the full pattern. **Infection outcomes remain the principal evidence gap.** BSI and IFI carry VERY LOW certainty. Both show substantial discordance between Bayesian and frequentist estimators, and both have extreme heterogeneity. Dedicated prospective studies with standardised endpoint definitions are needed. **C2 NRM is no longer gradeable.** Arm classification corrections reduced k to 2. The steroid mediation pattern observed in C1 NRM (OR 0.88 → M2 OR 0.90) remains the best available evidence for the GVHD→steroid→NRM causal chain. ::: {.callout-tip} ## Post-Block-9 GRADE Changes - C2 NRM: removed (k = 2 after arm reclassification) - C2 BSI: removed (k = 3 Mantel-Haenszel was not formally gradeable) - C2 CMV: still VERY LOW; reasoning revised from "direction reversal" to "gradient pattern" - C1 IFI: k decreased (8 → 6), but CrI now excludes null; τ = 1.64 warrants extreme caution - All other outcomes: certainty unchanged :::
